stack.name: SOURCE INVENTORY
stack.fault: Which physical volumes exist and which tome each holds. FAULT: a book attested by a volume that cannot contain it (an NT-only witness claiming Genesis), or an admitted volume that is a duplicate rendering.

stack.name: PAGE ADDRESSING
stack.fault: page → (book, chapter). FAULT: a chapter with no page at all; a page addressed to the wrong chapter. The DP is MONOTONE, so a single false heading does not mis-label one page — it makes every chapter between the true and false position unreachable (defect #9).

stack.name: TOME MAP
stack.fault: The derived per-volume coverage claim. FAULT: divergence from V1. It is DERIVED from addressing, so it can never be fed back as a prior — that would be a self-fulfilling loop (see `tome_prior`).

stack.name: PINNING / BODY ISOLATION
stack.fault: Which lines of a page are body, and which chapter owns them. FAULT: a chapter's line range truncated (defect #8) or over-offered; marginal-column apparatus concatenated INTO a body line by the line builder, so it cannot be separated downstream by role.

stack.name: VERSE LOCALIZATION
stack.fault: chapter body → per-verse spans. FAULT: no span for a verse present on the page (a MISS); a span that stops short or swallows its neighbour.

stack.name: RECOGNITION
stack.modules: reocr_core (kraken base / R1 / R2 fine-tuned) · r3_route (olmOCR)
stack.fault: Glyph accuracy on the span's pixels. FAULT: substituted tokens. This is the ONLY layer a better recognizer can fix, which is why everything above it must be excluded first.

stack.name: REFERENCE
stack.modules: s_dismas (archaic, preeminent) · odr_com (archaic backfill) · janvier/sabates_a (modern grid)
stack.fault: What the verse is compared against, and the versification grid it is cut on. FAULT: a locus the reference does not carry; a versification offset (the Psalm superscription shift).

stack.name: GATING / SCORING
stack.fault: archaic-preeminent identity scoring and the ≥0.90 bar. FAULT: a metric that consults a set the label helped build (defect #7), or any rule that converts a below-bar unit into an accepted one.

stack.name: REPORTING / VERSIONING
stack.fault: What is published and how versions are compared. FAULT: a stale or circular figure persisted where a later reader will quote it.

A.label: EXTRA tokens
A.note: interleaved apparatus / neighbouring-chapter bleed inside the span

B.label: MISSING tokens
B.note: the span stops short of the verse — truncation or a bad cut

C.label: SUBSTITUTED tokens
C.note: the words are there but misrecognised — recognizer territory

D.label: near-miss
D.note: below the bar with no dominant error mode; usually accumulated glyph noise

E.label: no archaic reference
E.note: nothing to compare against — the verse cannot pass at any quality
